notes: Shopify store. robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow (checked first); HTTP-tier access (curl, no JS needed) was sufficient for the whole company - never escalated past tier 1. Discovery: pulled the full collections catalog via /collections.json?limit=250 paginated across 12 pages (2,879 total collections, exhaustive), scanned all titles/handles against the full holiday vocabulary in rules/seasonal.md SS3 (Christmas/Xmas, Halloween, Diwali/Deepavali, Easter, Valentine, Thanksgiving, New Year, Holi/Rakhi/Eid/Navratri/Dussehra/other Indian festivals, Mother's/Father's Day, St. Patrick's, Independence Day, Black Friday, Fall/Autumn/Winter/Spring/Summer, wreath/ornament/stocking/pumpkin/skull/etc. product-level terms). Also checked the rendered main nav (id=main-navbar, ~62 top-level/section labels - no Gifts/Holiday/seasonal branch present at all), secondary navbar, footer, and /pages/trends-and-inspiration for any seasonal entry point; none found - all seasonal collections on this site are currently unlinked from live navigation (expected for a Sept visit ahead of Nov/Dec season and after Halloween-adjacent promo). Confirmed each candidate collection is still a real, live, indexed page (not orphaned/removed) via the sitemap (sitemap_collections_1.xml/_2.xml both list the handles). No Diwali, Easter, Thanksgiving, New Year, or any Indian-festival collection exists anywhere in the 2,879-collection catalog (checked exhaustively, zero matches) - recorded as genuinely absent, not unchecked. QTY METHOD: the collections.json 'products_count' field proved inflated on every candidate when cross-checked (matches the known Shopify-count-unreliable pattern), e.g. christmas-ornaments field=46 vs. full /collections/<handle>/products.json enumeration=24 (page 2 confirmed empty); used the full products.json enumeration (structured API count, paged to exhaustion) as the authoritative qty for every row instead of the field. EXCLUDED as non-holiday: 'Seasonal Living' (7 sub-collections, e.g. seasonal-living-bar/dining-room/lighting/lounge/seating/sofas/tables) - this is a furniture BRAND name (Seasonal Living outdoor furniture), not a holiday, and all show 0 products; 'Santa & Cole' - a lighting brand, coincidental name match, not Halloween; the entire non-holiday Gifts family (Gifts, Gifts for Men, Gifts for Women/Her, Gifts for Grads, Gifts for the Host, Gifts for the Minimalist, Gifts for Yourself, Gifts Under $100/$199/$300, Gifts for Foodies & Bartenders, Gifts for the Bartender, Tom Dixon Gifts, Ultra Fantasy Gifts, Wedding Gifts, Corporate Gifting, Housewarming Gifts, Quick-Ship Gifts) - recipient/price/occasion-neutral gift categories, none tied to a specific holiday/festival per rules SS3, correctly excluded per the same logic already applied project-wide; 'The Fall Edit: Cozy Materials & Inviting Details' (fall-materials-textures, 111/107 products) - despite Fall/Autumn being a valid SS3 seasonal event in principle, this page's own title/H1 reads as an editorial marketing 'edit' (article + Edit + colon + descriptive subtitle), structurally matching the explicit SS4 exclusion pattern (Lookbook/Inspiration-style framing) rather than a plain taxonomic category name like 'Halloween Decor' - treated as a marketing page, excluded; 'Black Friday Editor's Picks' (black-friday-editors-picks, 120 products via enumeration) - Black Friday is a valid SS3 seasonal event in principle, and this is a real, indexed PLP, but direct product-level evidence (sampled 20 products via products.json) showed every item carrying a compare_at_price roughly 15-20% above the current price, i.e. this is a discount/markdown showcase, functionally equivalent to the explicitly-excluded 'Black Friday Sale' example in SS4, not a standing product-type category - excluded on that concrete evidence rather than name alone. INCLUDED rows verified as genuine PLPs (own H1, own URL, real enumerable product list, sampled product titles checked for topical relevance): Halloween Decor (247 products; sampled titles include Skull Kintsugi/Skull Outdoor Stool/Skull Nano Planter/Skull Candle plus general dark-aesthetic decor and furniture - the site itself brands and names the whole collection 'Halloween Decor', satisfying the site-association test even though many included pieces are otherwise-normal decor curated for the mood); Christmas Ornaments (24 products; baubles, tree-top star, bells, cones - unambiguous); Valentine's Day Gifts (129 products); Mother's Day Gifts (190 products) and Father's Day Gifts (117 products) - both explicitly in-scope per the task's Mother's/Father's Day reminder, evaluated as genuine standing PLPs with real enumerable product lists, not excluded as 'universal gift occasions'; Holiday Decor (80 products) - MANUAL REVIEW flag: the site's own label is the generic 'Holiday Decor' rather than a name explicitly containing 'Christmas'; classified as Christmas per rules SS3's own discovery vocabulary (which lists 'Holiday Decor, Holiday Decorations' under the Christmas section) and supported by a sampled product mix skewing winter/Christmas (gnome stools, a Skier Figurine, a Bear Family figurine, tealight holders) rather than Halloween/other; no exact same-holiday duplicate collection exists to merge it with (Christmas Ornaments and Holiday Decor returned zero product-ID overlap when checked directly). No grouping/parent rows needed - none of the found categories share a live parent node in the taxonomy (each is a standalone leaf collection with no unifying 'Christmas'/'Holiday Shop' root on this site). No PDP pages were opened at any point; all classification came from collection-level pages, collections.json, and products.json enumeration.
